topics.title: Finding Mean (Average)
topics.concept:
What is Mean (Average)?

The mean is the fair share — if you add all numbers and split equally among all items.

Formula:

Mean = Sum of all values ÷ Number of values

Steps:

  1. Add up all numbers (find the sum)
  2. Count how many numbers (n)
  3. Divide sum by count

Example: Find mean of 5, 7, 12, 8

  • Sum = 5 + 7 + 12 + 8 = 32
  • Count = 4 numbers
  • Mean = 32 ÷ 4 = 8
topics.visual:
MEAN AS "FAIR SHARE":

    Data: 4, 6, 8, 10
    
    Step 1: Stack all values:
        │
        │   ■ (10)
        │   ■ (8)
        │   ■ (6)
        │   ■ (4)
        └─────
    
    Step 2: Level them out (each gets same):
        │ ■ ■ ■ ■
        │ ■ ■ ■ ■
        │ ■ ■ ■ ■
        │ ■ ■ ■ ■
        └─────
    
    Each column has 7 → Mean = 7


MEAN ON A NUMBER LINE:

    Data: 2, 4, 9
    
    Sum = 15
    Count = 3
    Mean = 15 ÷ 3 = 5
    
    <---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|--->
        2       4       5       9
                       ↑
                      Mean
    Values balance around 5: (5-2)=3, (5-4)=1, (9-5)=4; 3+1=4 ✓

examples.problem: Maria's test scores: 85, 92, 78, 95, 90. What is her average?
The mean of 4 numbers is 15. Three numbers are 10, 18, and 14. Find the fourth.
examples.solution:
• Sum of all 4 = mean × count = 15 × 4 = 60
  • Sum of known = 10 + 18 + 14 = 42
  • Fourth = 60 - 42 = 18
  • Answer: 18

recap: Can be a decimal (not necessarily a data value)
Use to find missing number: total - known sum

topics.title: Median & Mode Introduction
topics.concept:
Median (Middle Value)

The median is the middle number when data is arranged in order.

Steps to Find Median:

  1. Arrange numbers from smallest to largest
  2. If odd count → middle number
  3. If even count → average of two middle numbers

Example (Odd): 3, 7, 9, 11, 15 → median = 9

Example (Even): 3, 7, 9, 11 → median = (7+9)/2 = 8

Mode (Most Frequent)

The mode is the value that appears most often.

  • One mode: 2, 2, 3, 4, 5 → mode = 2
  • Two modes (bimodal): 1, 1, 2, 2, 3 → modes = 1 and 2
  • No mode: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 → no mode
topics.visual:
FINDING MEDIAN:

    Data: 5, 2, 8, 1, 9
    
    Step 1: Order: 1, 2, 5, 8, 9
                 ↑
    Median = 5 (3rd number)


FINDING MEDIAN (EVEN COUNT):

    Data: 3, 6, 4, 9, 2, 7
    
    Step 1: Order: 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 9
                     ↑  ↑
                  Middle two: 4 and 6
    
    Median = (4 + 6) ÷ 2 = 5


MODE VISUAL (Bar Chart):

    Frequency
        │
      4│    ■
      3│    ■   ■
      2│    ■   ■   ■
      1│    ■   ■   ■   ■
        └───┬───┬───┬───┬───
            2   3   4   5   6
    
    Mode = 4 (appears 3 times, most frequent)

examples.solution:
• Count: 4 appears 3 times, 7 appears 2 times, others once
  • Most frequent = 4
  • Answer: 4

recap: Even count → average of two middle numbers
Data can have 1 mode, 2+ modes, or no mode
Mean, median, mode all describe "center" differently
